strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: proposal.apply can execute bounded homogeneous delete_file transactions under Rust-owned workspace mutation authority.
Delete transactions require WriteWorkspace permission, current approved unconsumed proposals, fresh preflight, expected target hash matching, safe path validation, and symlink rejection.
Apply results record bounded transaction and per-item delete evidence without raw file content, raw diffs, command output, environment, secrets, or absolute paths.
A headless caller can delete a coordinated file set and decide follow-up from durable per-item transaction evidence.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances controlled_workspace_tools with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: One authorized proposal.apply call can delete two to five approved existing files as a bounded delete_file transaction.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Single-file delete apply lacks transaction-level admission, shared authorization, per-item partial-failure evidence, and deterministic recovery input; replace/create transactions do not delete.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless Brownie cannot safely remove coordinated file sets under Rust-owned transaction control.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M23.2 recovered create transactions, M23.1 created files in transactions, and M22.2 routed completion evidence; this phase deletes existing files.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends the existing proposal.apply transaction_items request path.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. This reuses the existing apply result and transaction item result summary shape with delete fields on the existing item summary.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime admits homogeneous delete_file transactions, validates all delete items before mutation, deletes approved targets, verifies post-delete absence, and records bounded per-item results.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless automation can perform and recover from bounded multi-file deletion using durable transaction evidence rather than shell/git/manual sequencing.
answers.milestone_progress: This establishes the primary M24 delete transaction execution path and sets up a possible recovery phase.

exit_criteria: proposal.apply accepts two to five homogeneous delete_file transaction items using the existing transaction_items request path

Delete transactions require authorize=true, WriteWorkspace permission, current approved unconsumed proposals, expected_target_sha256, empty replacement_content, latest preflight, regular UTF-8 targets, protected path denial, parent traversal denial, and symlink rejection
No target is deleted when any pre-mutation admission precondition fails
Successful transactions delete only approved targets, sync parents where possible, verify post-delete absence per item, consume authorization, and record operation=delete_file_transaction
Partial delete failures record bounded per-item transaction evidence without attempting rollback recreation
Ledger and RPC results do not expose raw file content, raw diffs, prompts, provider responses, stdout/stderr, environment, secrets, absolute paths, or canonical paths
Existing single-file delete apply, replace-file transactions and recovery, and create-file transactions and recovery remain compatible
next_phase_candidate_notes: If M24.1 merges, assess whether bounded delete_file transaction recovery is a distinct remaining runtime capability; reject report/history/readiness/inspection-only followups.
